title: SLA Tracking and False Positive Formalization
goal: Track remediation deadlines per severity and surface overdue findings on the Dashboard. Require a documented reason when a finding is marked false positive.
scope: Two changes: (1) SLA TRACKING: add remediation_due_date (DATETIME nullable) and sla_breached (BOOLEAN default False) to Finding model. On finding creation, compute remediation_due_date based on severity using configurable SLA days from Settings (defaults: critical=1d, high=7d, medium=30d, low=90d, info=none). Add sla_days_critical/high/medium/low settings keys with defaults. Add a background check (or lazy compute on GET) that sets sla_breached=True when now > remediation_due_date and status not in (resolved, false_positive, accepted_risk). Add overdue_critical_count and overdue_high_count to the Dashboard API response. Show an Overdue badge on Dashboard with count and color. (2) FALSE POSITIVE FORMALIZATION: add false_positive_reason (TEXT nullable) and false_positive_confirmed_by (VARCHAR 255 nullable) to Finding model. In PATCH /api/v1/findings/{id}, when status is changed to false_positive, require false_positive_reason in the request body (return 422 if missing). In the Findings drawer UI, when operator selects false_positive status, show a text field Reason for false positive decision (required). Store false_positive_confirmed_by from the current actor.
generation_reason: No SLA enforcement means critical findings can sit open indefinitely with no alert. No false positive documentation means decisions are undocumented and unreviewable.

constraints.active_task_gate: Do not implement until single active task in NEXT_TASK.md.
constraints.scope_creep_guard: SLA and false positive fields only. No automated escalation emails in this slice.
